# Income tax and progressive rates (`progressive_income_tax`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/economy.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Economy & finance (`economy`)
- Deps: helped by census_vital_registration, double_entry, universal_schooling
- Core idea: Each person pays a share of his yearly income from land, trade, wages and investments, assessed from his own declaration checked by assessors, and where possible deducted at source by the one who pays the income (employer, bank, tenant). With marginal tax brackets the higher rate applies only to the part of income above each threshold, so a raise never lowers net income. It reaches wealth where it is, adjusts to ability to pay, and yields large sums in war. It needs written records of wages, rents and dividends, literate taxpayers and honest assessors; in a farming society without records, land and excise taxes are more practical.
- Pitfalls:
  - Confusing marginal and average rates: believing a higher bracket taxes the whole income at the higher rate
  - Relying on self-declaration without withholding or checks: evasion is massive (Pitt's 1799 tax)
  - Setting very high rates where capital and people can leave
  - Proposing it in a society without paper records and money wages: it cannot be assessed
  - Thinking income tax is ancient: tithes and Islamic zakat were levies on produce or wealth, and a general income tax dates from 1799
- History: islamic: 7th c. – zakat, a 2.5 % levy on savings and trade goods above a minimum (nisab), with fixed rates on crops and herds; europe: 1427 – Florence's catasto taxes declared wealth with allowances for dependants; 1480–1481 graduated assessment; 1495 flat decima on property income; 1500 the decima scalata is renewed after debate in 1499; 1799 Pitt's income tax with a graduated scale up to 10 %; 1803 Addington's schedules and deduction at source; 1842 Peel; 1891 Prussia's progressive income tax; india: 1860 – first income tax in British India; east_asia: 1887 – Japan introduces a progressive income tax; americas: 1861 – US Civil War income tax; 1913 Sixteenth Amendment
- Read:
  - Luciano Pezzolo, Fiscal Tradition and Innovation in Italy, 1350–1650 (2022)
  - Nikola Regent, Guicciardini’s La Decima scalata: The First Treatise on Progressive Taxation (2014)
  - Martin Daunton, Trusting Leviathan: The Politics of Taxation in Britain, 1799–1914 (2001)
  - Kenneth Scheve & David Stasavage, Taxing the Rich (2016)
  - Adam Smith, An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776), book V ch. 2
